title: Genes and Mutations
seo_title: Grade 8 Genes and Mutations Worksheets: DNA, Proteins, Traits and Mutation Effects
standard_text: Develop and use a model to describe why structural changes to genes (mutations) located on chromosomes may affect proteins and may result in harmful, beneficial, or neutral effects to the structure and function of the organism.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on genes and mutations (NGSS MS-LS3-1): how genes code for proteins and traits, substitutions, insertions and deletions, and harmful, beneficial and neutral mutations. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_sub: A mutation changes a gene's instructions. It may change the protein and the trait, with harmful, beneficial or neutral effects.
body_html:
How to think about it

Chromosomes are made of DNA. A gene is a section of DNA with instructions for making a protein, and proteins shape traits.

gene → protein → trait

A mutation is a change in the DNA sequence: a substitution (one base swapped), an insertion (a base added) or a deletion (a base removed). A mutation can change the protein and the trait. The effect can be harmful, beneficial or neutral, often depending on the environment.

Example

ATGCCA becomes ATGACA. Type?

Same length, one base changed.

Answer: substitution

Example

A mutation lets insects survive a pesticide. Effect?

Helps survival.

Answer: beneficial

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all mutations are harmful.
  • Thinking a mutation in a body cell, like a skin cell, is passed to children.
  • Mixing up the order: genes code for proteins, not the other way around.

faq.q: What is the relationship between genes and proteins?
faq.a: A gene is a section of DNA that carries the instructions for making a protein. Proteins help determine an organism's traits.
No. Mutations can be harmful, beneficial or neutral. The effect often depends on the organism's environment.

faq.q: What are the main types of gene mutations?
faq.a: Substitution (one base is replaced), insertion (a base is added) and deletion (a base is removed).
